March: Spring Arrives on Two Wheels

March marks the real start of the UK motorcycle season. Clocks go forward at the end of the month, daylight stretches past 6pm, and the first genuinely warm days appear. It's still changeable — March can deliver snow, gale-force winds, and blazing sunshine in the same week — but the riding opportunities are real and growing.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 5-11°C. Warm spells can reach 15°C in the south. Cold snaps can still bring frost and even snow.
  • Daylight: From 6:45am-5:45pm at the start to 6:30am-7:30pm by month's end (after clocks change).
  • Roads: Councils reduce gritting as temperatures rise. Watch for residual grit and winter debris on B-roads.

March Riding Highlights

  • Daffodils: Wales and the Lake District are carpeted in daffodils through March. Wordsworth country around Ullswater is particularly beautiful.
  • Lambing season: Adorable but hazardous. Lambs are unpredictable near roads. Slow down in farming areas — this is their space.
  • First day rides: The first proper day ride of the year after winter always feels special. Plan a modest route (80-120 miles) and ease back into riding fitness.

March Hazards

  • Variable grip: Tyres may be cold and pressures low after winter storage. Check pressures and ride gently for the first few miles.
  • Rusty riding skills: After weeks or months off the bike, your skills need warming up. Take it easy for the first few rides of the season. Smooth inputs, moderate speed, and conscious attention to technique.
  • Other road users: Drivers haven't seen motorcycles for months. Their "looked but didn't see" reflex hasn't kicked in yet. Ride defensively.
March riding wisdom: dress for winter, ride like it's spring, hope for summer. The temperature on a motorcycle at speed is always colder than it looks from the kitchen window. Don't be caught out by a sunny morning that turns into a freezing afternoon.

March Preparation Checklist

Before your first proper ride of the season, work through this checklist: check oil level and condition, inspect brake pads for wear, test all lights and indicators, check tyre pressures and tread depth, lubricate chain and check tension, and verify that all fluid levels are correct.

Test your riding gear too. Reproofing waterproof textiles with Nikwax or similar restores water resistance that degrades over time. Check the condition of your gloves, boots, and helmet lining. Replace anything that's worn out — starting the season with reliable gear gives you confidence in any conditions. Read our UK Motorcycle Riding in May: Peak Spring Perfection guide for more. Read our Spring Motorcycle Destinations UK: March to May Riding Guide guide for more. Read our UK Motorcycle Riding in January: Winter Riding Guide guide for more.

Clocks go forward at the end of March, stretching daylight to roughly 6:30am-7:30pm.
Lambing season makes lambs unpredictable near roads, so slow down in farming areas.
Tyres and skills are cold and rusty after winter, so ride gently and check pressures for the first few miles.
Daffodils in Wales and the Lake District, especially around Ullswater, mark the season's real start.

faq.q: When does the UK motorcycle season really start?
faq.a: March marks the real start. The clocks go forward at the end of the month, daylight stretches past 6pm and the first genuinely warm days appear. It remains changeable, with snow, gales and sunshine all possible in one week, but the riding opportunities are real and growing. A modest 80 to 120-mile first ride is a good way to ease back in.

faq.q: What are the main hazards of riding in March?
faq.a: Variable grip is the biggest issue: tyres may be cold and pressures low after winter storage, so check pressures and ride gently for the first few miles. Your own skills will be rusty too, so use smooth inputs and moderate speed. Drivers have not seen motorcycles for months, so their looked-but-did-not-see reflex has not returned, meaning you must ride defensively.

faq.q: Why should I slow down for lambing season?
faq.a: March is lambing season and lambs are adorable but genuinely hazardous. They are unpredictable near roads and can dart out without warning, and ewes may follow them. Slow right down through farming areas and rural lanes because this is their space. It is one of the charming but demanding features of riding through the British countryside in early spring.

faq.q: What should I check before my first March ride?
faq.a: Work through a pre-season checklist: oil level and condition, brake pad wear, all lights and indicators, tyre pressures and tread depth, chain lubrication and tension, and fluid levels. Test your gear too, reproofing waterproof textiles with a product like Nikwax and checking gloves, boots and helmet lining. Reliable gear gives confidence in changeable March conditions.

faq.q: Where are the best March destinations?
faq.a: Wales and the Lake District are carpeted in daffodils through March, with Wordsworth country around Ullswater especially beautiful. Sheltered, lower routes in the south and west offer the mildest conditions. Remember the old wisdom: dress for winter, ride like it is spring and hope for summer, because it is always colder at speed than it looks from the kitchen window.
